![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14057969/assets/7fc64a261de4941b5ad35b8308b82b0f51c6b6bfbde177aafd793a0a0ac99da6.png)

Which of the following gives the line integral ${\int }_{C}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is the quarter of the ellipse $4{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}=12,$ located in the second quadrant, shown above?
worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{2}^{2}}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $\sqrt{3}$ and $2,$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le t\le \pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-\sqrt{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3{sin}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+3({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+3}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)={x}^{2}y,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =3{cos}^{2}⁡t\cdot 2\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\  & =6\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }6\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+3}\,\text{d}t \\  & =6{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t{cos}^{2}⁡t\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+3}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
